corpus: what a NAMED university pays a National Merit standing (RFC 243, slice test/08/the-psat-is-money, brief 0010)
method: One curation pass on 2026-09-25 fetched each institution's OWN scholarship page directly over HTTPS with a browser User-Agent and redirects followed, and quoted it. No aggregator, no blog, no model memory: a third-party list was used only to FIND a candidate page, never to source a figure. Every unit_id is either reused verbatim from db/seed/automatic-awards/awards.csv (where the school already appears there) or resolved against that school's own NCES College Navigator entry and confirmed by name. Every source_url returned HTTP 200 to this run's own fetch. link-status.csv was produced with `nix develop -c bin/check-link` from the worktree and mapped to RFC 200's vocabulary (2xx/3xx found, 404/410 not_found, anything else unknown).

counts.note_on_exact_figures: 8 of the 16 paying schools print a figure this corpus could parse into award_per_year_usd or award_total_usd. The other 8 price the award in WORDS (full tuition, cost of attendance, a component list, a ceiling or a range) and are stored that way, per the RFC's rule that the words are required and the numbers optional.

quoting_rules: Every *_as_published cell is the publisher's own words from the page fetched on 2026-09-25, trimmed.
Where the award is published as a BULLET LIST or a TABLE, the items are joined with '; ' (or ', ' inside one table row) and nothing else is changed: no word is added, removed or reordered.

Footnote markers ('*', '**') are dropped from a quote only where the marker is DECORATION. A marker that BINDS a footnote to a value is KEPT, on both the value and the footnote, because dropping it silently re-scopes the publisher's caveat from one component to the whole award - a different claim from the one they made. Florida State's out_of_state row is the case: "a $16,000*, Vires scholarship" and "*Admitted first-year students starting Fall 2024." are both quoted with their marker, exactly as the page prints them.
No figure, date or sentence in this file was written from memory or inferred. Where the page publishes no figure, the numeric columns are empty and the words carry the award.

date_rule.rule: A deadline DATE is filled only where the page prints the YEAR. A deadline the page states without a year (`by May 1`, `no later than Nov. 1`) is recorded in its *_as_published column with the date column left empty.
date_rule.why: The year is derivable from the cycle, but deriving it would put a date in the row that is not on the page. One row (The University of Alabama) prints its year and is the only row with first_choice_deadline filled.

entry_year_rule.rule: entry_year is the entry cycle THE PAGE DESCRIBES, named by its first calendar year. A page still describing Fall 2026 entry on 2026-09-25 is a STALE cycle and is NOT a row; it is listed under read_but_not_seeded.

award_kind_judgements.why: the page hedges with "may qualify" but uses no consideration, competition or committee language for the National Merit award; the hedge survives verbatim in award_as_published. A reviewer who reads "may qualify" as consideration should flip this to competitive.

the award is stated as an entitlement, but it is conditional on being admitted to and enrolling in Barrett, The Honors College - a separate application. The condition is inside the quoted sentence rather than lost in the kind column.

figures_deliberately_not_parsed.why: the page's only dollar figures ("approximately $22,000 for Idaho residents", "over $85,000") are keyed to "the 2026-27 academic year", a cycle earlier than this row's. The undated guarantee sentence is quoted instead and every numeric column is empty.
"more than $25,000 per year" is a floor, not a figure; writing 25000 would understate it and read as exact.
"up to $8,000" and "full non-resident portion of tuition plus $4,000 per year" are a ceiling and a component, not the award's value.
"can range between $16,000 - $25,000 per year" is a range.
the page publishes each component's annual and total amount but no package total; summing them would be our arithmetic, not theirs.
the package is tuition, housing and two cash components with no published total.
